title: A photon above the threshold
hook: Change frequency above the threshold and predict maximum electron kinetic energy.
misconception: maximum electron kinetic energy stays fixed when frequency above the threshold doubles.
objective: Apply K_max = h(f − f₀) to compare maximum electron kinetic energy when frequency above the threshold changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal photoelectric model for one fixed material, K_max = h(f − f₀). When frequency above the threshold doubles, maximum electron kinetic energy becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model K_max = h(f − f₀); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal photoelectric model for one fixed material, with a nonzero initial result. If frequency above the threshold triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on maximum electron kinetic energy?
recall.why: Apply K_max = h(f − f₀) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
